subjects.displayTitle: The Manifestations: one light, distinct missions
subjects.introduction: The sun does not rise from the same point each morning, yet no one mistakes it for a different sun. Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá use that observation to hold unity and difference together: the Manifestations are mirrors, each with a distinct individuality, a prescribed mission and a particular Revelation, while the light reflected in them is one. Their laws differ because the ages they addressed differed; some founded a dispensation while others promulgated its laws; they vary, Bahá’u’lláh says, in the intensity of their revelation and the potency of their light, even as the Qur’an states that some messengers were caused to excel others [1]. In their second station they show utter servitude and self-effacement, which keeps the comparison from becoming a contest among religious communities. Reported conversations add analogies of lamps, moons and stars and reflections on historical circumstance, each to be read in its setting. The path leads on into progressive revelation, the twofold station of the Manifestation, and the question of their oneness or innumerability.
subjects.arc: Start with recognition across changing horizons, distinguish mission from source, explore the solar analogies, and end with servitude and historical conditions.

order.why: Give unity and individuality a clear image in different mirrors.
shortened: The Manifestations of God are like so many different mirrors, as They each have Their own distinct individuality, but that which is reflected in these mirrors is one and the same sun. Thus, it is evident that the reality of Christ is different from that of Moses.

order.why: Open with the familiar act of recognizing a sunrise in a changing place.
Read the fuller account of the two stations. Return to the common names and attributes alongside intensity of revelation. Set these distinctions beside complete servitude.
shortened: Nay, all the Prophets of God, His well-favored, His holy, and chosen Messengers, are, without exception, the bearers of His names, and the embodiments of His attributes. They only differ in the intensity of their revelation, and the comparative potency of their light. Even as He hath revealed: "Some of the Apostles We have caused to excel the others."

The other is the station of distinction, and pertaineth to the world of creation and to the limitations thereof. In this respect, each Manifestation of God hath a distinct individuality, a definitely prescribed mission, a predestined Revelation, and specially designated limitations. Each one of them is known by a different name, is characterized by a special attribute, fulfills a definite Mission, and is entrusted with a particular Revelation.

Viewed in the light of their second station -- the station of distinction, differentiation, temporal limitations, characteristics and standards -- they manifest absolute servitude, utter destitution and complete self-effacement.

order.why: Explicitly distinguishes the station of unity in revelation from differing prophetic ranks in the station of distinction.
Connect differing laws with the requirements of their ages.
shortened: These principles and laws, these firmly-established and mighty systems, have proceeded from one Source, and are rays of one Light. That they differ one from another is to be attributed to the varying requirements of the ages in which they were promulgated.
In truth I say, and for the sake of God I declare: This Servant, this Wronged One, is abashed to claim for Himself any existence whatever, how much more those exalted grades of being!

order.why: Name the differences in words, deeds, and commandments.
Distinguish founding a dispensation from promulgating its laws.
Consider the prescribed measure of revelation.
Relate distinct acts and messages to apparent difference in greatness.
Explore the seasonal analogy and its scriptural allusion.
Read the further comparison of the sun’s influences.
shortened: The sun hath ever had diverse manifestations and influences. The sun that riseth from the sign of Aquarius is, upon its appearance, effaced before the sun that ariseth from the sign of Leo. Every person of insight observeth countless differences.

order.why: Consider the imagery of a particular divine horizon.
Explore variation through several images of light.
Return to the shared aim behind differing names.
Read the extended historical account with its reported cultural judgments intact.
shortened: Each Manifestation was alike great in himself, each spoke with the same authority, each alike breathed the spirit of God. The same fundamental truth underlies the doctrines of each. The differences between them were not in themselves, but in the evolutionary stages of the peoples whom they taught. When Christ appeared, the people among whom he came were in a low state of intelligence there was little or no discussion of abstruse questions among them. Buddha, though earlier, came to a part of the world where civilisation was much more advanced, which was ripe in philosophical and metaphysical speculations. Mahomet found wild tribes and hordes of uncivilised barbarians.

On the one hand, each of these great teachers had to meet a problem peculiar to himself-that of guiding and satisfying his contemporaries and associates; and, on the other, the condition of the world's advancement in general-the state of communication between different parts of the world-was such that the teachings of each were confined to the people of that region to which they came and for whom they were especially adapted.

order.why: Examine the developmental analogy in its reported form.
Consider the reported account of heralds and the interval before another Manifestation.
Hear the explanation offered in a conversation about Christ.
Read the stronger claim concerning Christ and Bahá’u’lláh. Consider the explicit distinction involving prophets of the House of Israel.
shortened: Know that the attributes of perfection, the outpourings of divine grace, and the effulgences of divine revelation shine resplendent in all the Manifestations of God, but that the all-encompassing Word of God--Christ--and His Most Great Name--Baha'u'llah--have appeared with a revelation beyond all conception. For not only do they possess all the perfections of the former Manifestations, but they also evince beyond those such perfections as to make all others even as their followers.

Pause then to reflect upon the difference between the virtues and perfections of Christ and the splendours and effulgences of Baha'u'llah on the one hand, and the virtues of the Prophets of House of Israel, such as Ezekiel or Samuel, on the other. All were the recipients of divine revelation, but between them there is an immeasurable distance.

order.why: Widen the horizon beyond a fixed number of appearances.
Close the linked readings with dependence upon God.
shortened: If I call upon Thee by Thy Name, the All-Possessing, I am compelled to recognize that He Who holdeth in His hand the immediate destinies of all created things is but a vassal dependent upon Thee, and is the creation of but a word proceeding from Thy mouth.

order.why: Retain the reported comparison involving the title Seal of the Prophets.
Read the separately supplied statement about Christ and Bahá’u’lláh.
shortened: Verse 27: The Lamb's Book of life is only one book that of the Lamb (Abdul-Baha). Chapter 12, verse 10: Christ and Baha'u'llah are mentioned as being One in degree of power.

order.why: End with the relation of differing reflection to conditions and circumstances.

questions: How does the changing place of sunrise help explain recognition of unity amid religious difference?
What distinctions do these readings make among individuality, mission, revealed law, and spiritual source?
How does the Qur’anic passage on differences among messengers illuminate the solar and mirror analogies used here?
What can historical circumstances explain about differences in religious teaching, and what questions remain beyond such an explanation?
How might this understanding change a conversation with someone whose religious language or practice differs from one’s own?

neighbors.invitation: Distinguish differences among Manifestations from the distinction between a Manifestation and other beings.
Explore the covenant linking one promised revelation to another.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 2:253 · Differences among messengers
references.note: The verse speaks of distinctions among messengers, divine speech, and the support given to Jesus, before turning to conflict among later followers. Compare the verse with the compilation’s account of distinct missions and a shared source; the Bahá’í exposition adds an interpretive framework of its own.

subjects.displayTitle: The Manifestation: the source and the reflection
subjects.introduction: A mirror can be polished until it blazes, and it still is not the sun. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá uses that difference to speak of the Manifestation of God, whose reality is like the sun that must give light by its very nature and cannot be compared with anything that merely reflects it. Such a Being eats, sleeps and grows tired like anyone else, and Bahá’u’lláh asks forgiveness of those who looked no further and took Him for one like themselves. He is the educator humanity cannot do without, ordering its material affairs, opening its mind to science, and breathing into hearts a life whose effects remain thousands of years later. A disciple may advance without end and never become Christ; a hard stone does not become a ruby, and this limit is the ground on which growth is possible. Jesus’ image of the vine and its branches holds the same closeness and dependence together [1]. The way continues toward the Manifestation as educator, the Perfect Man, and the authority that belongs to His station.
subjects.arc: Begin with the sun and its reflections, examine education and recognition, then hold the promise of human growth beside the limits of identity.

order.why: Consider spiritual distinction through its capacity to gather and shelter others.
shortened: But in this age of splendours, this era of God, the pre-eminent Personage, the luminous Orb, the chosen Individual will shine out with such perfections and such power as ultimately to dazzle the minds of every community and group. And since such a Personage is superior to all others in spiritual perfections and heavenly attainments, and is indeed the focal centre of divine blessings and the pivot of the circle of light, He will encompass all others, and there is no doubt whatsoever that He will shine out with such power as to gather every soul into His sheltering shade.

order.why: Open with the sun’s inherent light and the limits of comparison.
shortened: But the individual reality of the Manifestations of the All-Merciful is a sanctified reality, and it is so because it surpasses in essence and in attributes all created things. It is like the sun, which, by virtue of its inherent disposition, must inevitably produce light, and cannot be compared to any satellite.

order.why: Ask how familiar bodily conditions can obscure a spiritual claim.
Explore the work of a universal educator in material, intellectual, and spiritual life.
shortened: It is therefore clear and evident that man stands in need of an educator. This educator must undeniably be perfect in every way and distinguished above all men. For if he were like others he could never be their educator, particularly since he must at once be their material, human and spiritual educator.

Our meaning is that the universal Educator must be at once a material, a human and a spiritual educator, and, soaring above the world of nature, must be possessed of another power, so that He may assume the station of a divine teacher. Were He not to wield such a celestial power, He would not be able to educate, for He would be imperfect Himself. How then could He foster perfection?

order.why: Situate the Manifestation within the wider reflection of divine attributes.
shortened: Man, the noblest and most perfect of all created things, excelleth them all in the intensity of this revelation, and is a fuller expression of its glory. And of all men, the most accomplished, the most distinguished and the most excellent are the Manifestations of the Sun of Truth. Nay, all else besides these Manifestations live by the operation of their Will, and move and have their being through the outpourings of their grace.

order.why: Turn from external comparison to the Manifestation’s own person as evidence.
shortened: He Who is everlastingly hidden from the eyes of men can never be known except through His Manifestation, and His Manifestation can adduce no greater proof of the truth of His Mission than the proof of His own Person.

order.why: Explore the image of a book known through itself.
shortened: The Dawn hath appeared upon the Temple of Man. Verily this is the Book of the All-Merciful which was mentioned in the Scriptures of God, the Most High, the Most Great. Therein hath been inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen that which none knoweth save His Own Self, the All-Knowing.
This Book can only be known through itself, and this Man can only be known through his own self.

order.why: Read the direct challenge to treating the Manifestation as merely one’s equal.
shortened: Say: Seek ye forgiveness for what ye have thought concerning Him Who was among you but as one like yourselves. Though ye traverse the earth, ye shall find none like unto Him - and God is witness to this.

order.why: Affirm progress in discipleship while distinguishing it from becoming Christ.
Consider the reported account of divine appointment.
shortened: The other station is the special station of the Prophets, wherein God raiseth up an individual to the station of Prophethood without regard to capacity or qualification, as in the case of Moses, Christ, and Muhammad.

order.why: Read the further reported distinction between independent and dependent prophetic stations.
Close the linked readings with independence from belief or disbelief.
shortened: Their belief or disbelief in My Cause can neither profit nor harm Me. We summon them wholly for the sake of God. He, verily, can afford to dispense with all creatures.

order.why: Examine the threefold account of the divine revelator.
shortened: Man has two planes: the physical and the intellectual. The divine revelators have three: their physical condition, which is shared by all mankind - they eat, they sleep, they are sometimes ill, they become well again, they become fatigued, they undergo all that man can undergo; their intellectual degree and their holy reality which surrounds all beings and comprehends secrets.

Other men, although able to evolve to a high degree, are still in the second condition; this third state is alone partaken of by the divine messengers although great saints have attained extraordinary pre-eminence and reflect the splendor of the sun.

order.why: Explore the mirror as the focal point of education and new life.
shortened: Thus it is established that the true human bears the divine image and likeness, meaning they receive all divine perfections. Such a person is like a mirror, and divine bestowals are like the rays of the sun--all divine names and perfect attributes are reflected in this mirror.

Such a blessed soul is the center of spiritual manifestations, just as the sun is the center of light in the material world. This blessed soul breathes the breath of life into hearts, making souls spiritual, and divine bestowals shine forth in hearts. Such a blessed soul is the first teacher of the human world and the first manifestor to contingent beings.

order.why: Read the direct appeal to vision, utterance, and wisdom.
Consider the limits assigned to discipline and transformation.
shortened: Similarly, each type of human being has a spiritual station and progresses within his own rank and station. A dull person, no matter how much severe discipline he may undergo, no matter how much he may strive and be transformed, can never attain to the station of the Manifestations of Revelation and the Dawning-places of inspiration. The tree of Zaqqum cannot become a lofty palm, nor can the bitter colocynth yield sweet fruit. What fantasies are these, what strange conjectures, that people give ear to such delusions!

order.why: Distinguish the rank of independent Manifestations from other prophetic ranks.
shortened: As for the possibility of all creation attaining the station of the Prophets, this is not possible since creation has ranks - the lower cannot comprehend the higher - "He created you in degrees." A hard stone cannot become a red ruby, and pottery and shells cannot become brilliant pearls.

The believers of this Manifestation can reach the station of the Prophets of Israel, but not the Manifestations of Universal Divine Authority, for they were Universal Manifestations. In brief, the Universal Manifestations of God who shone forth independently have another station and another condition - no one can attain their station and rank.

order.why: Explains the essential infallibility and independent authority reserved to the universal Manifestations.
Recover the affirmation of endless progress within servitude.
shortened: So he who occupies the degree of servitude, no matter how far he may progress and acquire endless perfections, can never reach the degree of divine Lordship.
For example, Peter cannot become Christ. At most he can attain infinite perfections in the degrees of servitude; for every existing reality is capable of progress.

order.why: Keep the early translation’s metaphysical language in its supplied form.
shortened: Know thou that the Manifestation hath not emerged from the four elements, but rather is the Mystery of Oneness, the Pre-existent Essence, the Self-Subsisting Reality, and the Hidden Identity. Indeed, He cannot be known through aught else, nor can it be established for anyone that He hath appeared from the four elements, or from the basic substances mentioned in the language of the philosophers, or from the four natures - for all these were created by His command and will.

Were He to be known through any other than Himself, His essence could not be proven free from similitude, nor His being sanctified from likeness, nor His uniqueness from the manifestations of creation.

order.why: Read the twofold nature with its supplied explanatory note.
Explore the imagery of the greater and lesser worlds.
shortened: I testify that Thou wast a hidden Treasure wrapped within Thine immemorial Being and an impenetrable Mystery enshrined in Thine own Essence. Wishing to reveal Thyself, Thou didst call into being the Greater and the Lesser Worlds, and didst choose Man above all Thy creatures, and didst make Him a sign of both of these worlds, O Thou Who art our Lord, the Most Compassionate!

Thou didst raise Him up to occupy Thy throne before all the people of Thy creation. Thou didst enable Him to unravel Thy mysteries, and to shine with the lights of Thine inspiration and Thy Revelation, and to manifest Thy names and Thine attributes.

order.why: End in prayerful acknowledgment of the limits of description.
Consider the description of spiritual archetypes.

questions: How do the mirror and sun images hold together human spiritual potential and the unique station described in these selections?
What does the account of material, human, and spiritual education imply about the work of a Manifestation?
How might outward familiarity make recognition more difficult, and how could one investigate a claim without relying only on resemblance?
What does John’s image of vine and branches contribute to reflection on closeness, dependence, and spiritual fruitfulness?
How can acknowledgment of limits encourage growth rather than resignation or a diminished view of human dignity?

neighbors.invitation: Explore how distinct Manifestations can reflect one light while retaining their own individuality.
Follow the image of creatures as mirrors into the question of knowing God through signs.

references.label: 1 · John 15:1–5 · Vine and branches
references.note: Jesus describes the disciples’ fruitfulness through their abiding in him as branches in a vine. Compare the relation of participation and dependence with the sun and mirror images here, while preserving the Gospel’s particular account of Christ and discipleship.

subjects.introduction: Each letter of the revealed verses, Bahá’u’lláh says, carries a particular meaning in every one of the infinite worlds, and none has exhausted that treasury but God. Such richness invites discovery and also breeds contention. Bahá’u’lláh’s answer is not to close the text but to appoint a centre to which disagreements are referred: whoever fails to understand a verse is to ask its Source, and once two people quarrel to the point of alienation both are already wrong. Private conception may not be made the criterion of faith, and hearsay carries no authority beside a Tablet bearing the seal of Bahá’u’lláh or ‘Abdu’l-Bahá. Philip climbing into the chariot of an Ethiopian official puzzled by Isaiah shows the ancient human need for guided understanding, though it describes no Bahá’í institution [1]. None of this stifles study: individual understanding is encouraged, and authoritative exposition leads back into the original words. The road continues into Shoghi Effendi and the Guardianship, into the multiple meanings that scripture holds, and into the Covenant that keeps discovery from becoming division.
subjects.arc: Begin with the purpose of shared understanding, examine authority and evidence, distinguish reported sayings from authenticated text, and close with freedom for personal study.

order.why: Consider how differences are referred to a designated center.
Open with the depth of meaning and the wish to prevent discord.
shortened: And whatsoever of the divine verses they fail to comprehend, let them inquire of Him Who is their Source and Origin. The purpose of these words is that no discord may arise among the loved ones of God concerning the meaning of His words. Let them know that all divine utterances proceed from one Source and return unto Him. Beware lest ye find differences therein. Though outwardly revealed differently, in their inner reality they all return to and end in the same Word and the same Point.
Likewise, each of the divine letters and words is a treasury of innate knowledge, and none hath discovered what is treasured therein save God.

order.why: Connect interpretation with institutions and freedom of conscience.
shortened: But Baha'u'llah has shut the door to such differences. By His appointing the Expounder of the Holy Word, by setting up the Institution of the House of Justice, which is the legislative body elected by the people, and by enjoining non-interference in matters of belief and conscience, Baha'u'llah has barred the way that would lead to disruption in the Faith. He has even warned that if two persons disagreed with each other so as to create alienation, then both of them would be wrong and unjustified.

order.why: Acknowledge the limits of individual reasoning.
shortened: When we read the Book of God, the faculty of comprehension by which we form conclusions is reason. Reason is mind. If we are not endowed with perfect reason, how can we comprehend the meanings of the Word of God? Therefore, human reason, as already pointed out, is by its very nature finite and faulty in conclusions. It cannot surround the Reality Itself, the Infinite Word. Inasmuch as the source of traditions and interpretations is human reason, and human reason is faulty, how can we depend upon its findings for real knowledge?

order.why: Read the criticism of accumulated expectations concerning the Qá’im.
shortened: O 'Ali! Consider what they said concerning the Qa'im for twelve hundred years, and most of those who related and narrated traditions were among the divines. Nevertheless, not a single word thereof was adorned with the ornament of truth, as became evident on the Day of His manifestation.

order.why: Place the historical polemic about the sufficiency of a book in its original argument.
shortened: This conception of the sufficiency of the Book without an interpreter traceth its origin to 'Umar, who said "Sufficient unto us is the Book of God",  and who claimed that one stood in need of naught else--that is to say, no interpreter.  Thus did he lay the enduring foundations of contention and conflict, of enmity, fragmentation and division, among the friends and companions of the Prophet.  These words became the basis of all the iniquities, rebellions and transgressions, nay, of all the bloodshed that was to ensue.

order.why: Read the parallel warning concerning rejection of the interpreter.
shortened: Now "The Book of God suffices us" has been changed to "God has made all independent" and "return to the writings," meaning do not submit to the Interpreter, do not ask questions, do not act according to His good-pleasure, do not walk according to His guidance, and recognition is not necessary - be your own interpreter. And in this way the intent is to become free from the Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Examine the danger of making a private conception the criterion of faith.
shortened: The explicit text, the clear and manifest, the designated verses are present, yet the people of vain imaginings pursue the propagation of doubts, saying "Let us gather and exercise independent judgment in the Book of God, and make whatever we conceive in our imagination the foundation of the Faith of God." Vain indeed is that which they do!

order.why: Clarify the specific instruction about beliefs concerning ‘Abdu’l-Bahá.
Distinguish consultation on unknown matters from obedience to explicit text.
shortened: Now it appeareth that some of the friends hold particular views and interpret the explicit emphases differently, whereas that which floweth from this pen is the decisive Text of God. There can be no delay whatsoever in its execution, and this is one of the fundamental conditions of firmness in the Covenant. The friends of God must consult on matters that are unknown, but for matters issued from the Pen of the Covenant consultation is unnecessary - that is the Divine decree, for it is the explicit Text.

order.why: Read the explicit scope of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s interpretive authority. Make room for an explanation that does no harm.
Explains the explicit appointment and exclusive interpretive authority of the Center of the Covenant.
Return to unity as a criterion in the supplied account.
Introduce the concern for written authentication.
shortened: I have come to these parts and I find out that certain people have attributed to me certain statements of which I am innocent. Anybody who has an opinion and desires to circulate it will attribute it to me. Anyone quoting me must have authority written either with my own hand, or tablets signed with my seal. Otherwise, those statements do not belong to me. Every instruction, every teaching that I desire to spread, I will write with my own hand. You must know this generally. Never accept statements without my writing which is signed and sealed - any statement.

order.why: Consider the institutional role described for deductions.
Read the supplied account of originals, translations, and personal notes.
Consider the risk of unauthenticated narratives.
Distinguish corrected and authenticated talks from hearsay.
shortened: According to the Teachings of Baha'u'llah no authority can be attached to a mere hearsay, no matter through whom it may come. The Tablets that bear the seal or signature of Baha'u'llah and the Master are the only parts of the literature that have any authority and that constitute the basis of our belief. All other forms of literature may bear points of interest but they cannot be considered as authentic.

order.why: Read the extended explanation of that distinction.
shortened: This being a basic principle of the Faith we should not confuse Tablets that were actually revealed and mere talks attributed to the founders of the Cause. The first have absolute binding authority while the latter can in no way claim our obedience.

Those talks of the Master that were reviewed by Him corrected or in some other form considered authentic by Himself, such as the 'Some Answered Questions', these could be considered as Tablets and therefore be given the necessary binding power. All other talks such as are included in Ahmad's diary or the diary of pilgrims, do not fall under this category and could be considered only as interesting material to be taken for what they are worth.

order.why: Consider why repetition or the reporter’s reputation does not confer authority.
Read the counsel on the personal status of pilgrims’ notes.
Hold lack of binding authority beside the value of shared experience.
Acknowledge the possible inspiration of informal notes.
Affirm the place of individual study alongside authoritative interpretation.
Distinguish illuminating personal views from standards imposed on others.
End with interpretation that returns the reader to the revealed words.

questions: What different purposes are served by authoritative interpretation, personal understanding, and consultation?
How can a group welcome illuminating individual readings without allowing them to become standards others must accept?
What does the encounter between Philip and the Ethiopian reader suggest about asking for help, offering an explanation, and returning to the text?
How should a reader’s use of a moving personal recollection differ from their use of an authenticated text?
What practices could help a study group combine careful evidence, genuine exploration, and freedom from contention?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the connection between covenant, interpretation, and constructive deeds.
Try these distinctions on a difficult symbolic term that receives an explicit explanation.

references.label: 1 · Acts 8:26–35 · A reader asks for guidance
references.note: An Ethiopian official reading Isaiah invites Philip to help him understand whom the passage concerns; Philip explains it in relation to Jesus. Compare the value of guided reading with the compilation’s distinctions of authority, without treating this episode as a description of Bahá’í institutions.

subjects.displayTitle: The primordial covenant: remembering an answer
subjects.introduction: Have you forgotten that radiant morning, Bahá’u’lláh asks, when you stood beneath the tree of life and heard the words that bound you? The primordial covenant is a memory before all memories, the moment the Qur’an describes when the children of Adam testified to their Lord so that none could later plead ignorance [1]. Yet nearly everyone forgot, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá turns the ancient scene toward the present: the Day of Alast is the day of Manifestation, the hour when the Sun of Reality rises and every soul is asked the question again. The Báb adds that the question falls only on one who can choose, so the answer is an act of freedom. The images stay close to life, a cup whose wine is the covenant, a physician’s remedy that penetrates nerve and vein, and the promise is handed from Abraham to Moses to Christ and onward. Remembering such a covenant means more than recollection; it is translated into constructive deeds and the preservation of unity. The way leads to the centrality of the Covenant, to the reading of the Qur’an and the traditions, and to what preexistence means for a soul.
subjects.arc: Begin with the call to remember, connect timeless imagery to revelation and freedom, follow the chain of promise, and end with constructive action.

order.why: Open with the searching appeal to remember a forgotten covenant. Read the fuller image of remembered presence and a living heart.
shortened: Have ye forgotten that true and radiant morn, when in those hallowed and blessed surroundings ye were all gathered in My presence beneath the shade of the tree of life, which is planted in the all-glorious paradise? Awe-struck ye listened as I gave utterance to these three most holy words: O friends! Prefer not your will to Mine, never desire that which I have not desired for you, and approach Me not with lifeless hearts, defiled with worldly desires and cravings. Would ye but sanctify your souls, ye would at this present hour recall that place and those surroundings, and the truth of My utterance should be made evident unto all of you.

order.why: Make forgetfulness itself a subject of reflection.
shortened: For the covenant of "Am I not your Lord?" was well known and universal, and yet all forgot it, save for a handful of souls more scarce than the philosopher's stone.

order.why: Read the explicit explanation of the Day of Alast as the day of manifestation.
shortened: The Day of "Am I not?" is the Day of Manifestation. It is the hour of resurrection and revival. It is the time of the revelation of light. It is the moment of effulgence upon Sinai and the Mount. It is the Most Great Resurrection and the Supreme Catastrophe, when that Sun of Reality shines forth from the horizon of possibility and sheds its bounties upon the kingdoms of creation.
The realities of all that greatest cycle are resurrected on that blessed Day before the Merciful One, and all are included in the address "Am I not?"

order.why: Connect the divine question with the capacity to choose.
Hear the affirmative response become an act of recognition.
Place response within a prayer of gratitude for existence and guidance.
shortened: O my loving God! Through pure bounty didst Thou breathe into me the spirit of life, bestow upon me the robe of existence, give me to drink from the wellspring of guidance, cause mine ears to hear the call of 'Am I not your Lord?', make me to hear the cry of 'Glorified be my Lord, the Most Glorious!', grant me shelter beneath the Tree of Unity, give me to drink from the cup of the Covenant, single me out through Thy special favor, and make me successful in achieving a mighty triumph.

order.why: Explore the covenant described before the foundation of the world.
shortened: O Living Temple!  Through Thee have We gathered together all created things, whether in the heavens or on the earth, and called them to account for that which We had covenanted with them before the foundation of the world.

order.why: Trace its imagery through successive scriptures.
shortened: Fear God Who created you for His Revelation and took from you His covenant in the atoms of the Bayan, and before that in the atoms of the Furqan, and before that in the atoms of the Gospel, until it reacheth the primal atoms.

order.why: Consider creation and covenant in relation to a promised day.
Relates firmness in the Covenant to the primordial affirmation on the Day of Alast.
Introduce the promise of a coming revelation.
shortened: This notwithstanding the fact that all the Prophets of God, whenever made manifest unto the peoples of the world, have invariably foretold the coming of yet another Prophet after them, and have established such signs as would herald the advent of the future Dispensation.

order.why: Read the specified sequence of covenants and promised Manifestations.
shortened: Speak in accordance with the instructions written herein, and utter not even one word more: Abraham, on Him be peace, made a covenant concerning Moses and gave the glad-tidings of His coming. Moses made a covenant concerning the promised Christ, and announced the good news of His advent to the world. Christ made a covenant concerning the Paraclete and gave the tidings of His coming. The Prophet Muhammad made a covenant concerning the Bab, and the Bab was the One promised by Muhammad, for Muhammad gave the tidings of His coming. The Bab made a covenant concerning the Blessed Beauty, Baha'u'llah, and gave the glad-tidings of His coming for the Blessed Beauty was the One promised by the Bab. Baha'u'llah made a covenant concerning a Promised One Who will become manifest after one thousand or thousands of years.

order.why: Clarify the duration assigned to a prophetic mission.
shortened: And it is a basic principle of the Law of God that in every Prophetic Mission, He entereth into a Covenant with all believers---a Covenant that endureth until the end of that Mission, until the promised day when the Personage stipulated at the outset of the Mission is made manifest.

order.why: Turn toward the new covenant and its embrace.
shortened: O loved ones of God! The lamp of the Covenant is the light of the world, and its reality the gift of splendour; the star of the Testament is a shining moon, and the words traced by the Pen of the Most High a limitless ocean. The Lord, the All-Glorified, hath, beneath the shade of the Tree of Anisa (Tree of Life), made a new Covenant and established a great Testament. He hath summoned everyone to the loving embrace of His Beauty and announced unto all the revelation of His manifest verses.

order.why: Read the explanation relating the Hidden Word to Bahá’u’lláh’s covenant.
Keep the parallel commentary beside it.
Return to the language of a covenant without beginning or end.
shortened: The essence of all essences of eternity and everlasting purity is the Covenant of the Luminary of the horizons, which is from the day of "Am I not?" until the endless evening - it had no beginning and will have no end.

order.why: Hear praise for the covenant in the primal world.
shortened: They loosened their tongues in prayer and spoke in praise of their Lord, the Lord of the highest heavens, saying: "Glory be to our Most Glorious Lord Who took the Covenant in the primal world of atoms and blessed be His name in the next creation."

order.why: Explore the healing imagery and the cup of Alast.
shortened: The Ancient Physician healeth the nations with a sovereign remedy that penetrateth the nerves and veins - a pure, sufficient and healing elixir. It quickeneth the soul, its joy dispelleth grief; it revealeth the realities of divine mysteries; it illumineth the heart and maketh it merciful; it transformeth the breast into a divine mirror and the eyes into the seat of the presence of the Eternal.
Its chalice is the primal, timeless Cup of Alast; its wine is the crimson Wine of the Supreme Covenant; its Cupbearer is the Abha Beauty.

order.why: Consider the invitation to spiritual rapture.
Read the concise blessing upon those who respond.
shortened: Blessed are those persons who have become intoxicated from the joyous cup of the Primordial Covenant.

order.why: Connect rapture with knowledge and release from doubt.
shortened: You who are intoxicated with the wine of divine knowledge, seek the rapture of God's Covenant, that you may tell of the trust of the Primordial Day of "Am I not your Lord?", and be delivered from the fetters of the doubts of the people of allusions.

order.why: Include the supplied prayer concerning the covenant in the scriptures.
shortened: It behoveth every community that hath responded to My call, that hath turned unto Mine horizon, and directed its face toward the Qiblih of My loving-kindness, to beseech God at eventide and at dawn, and to say:

"O Lord of the lovers! I beseech Thee by Thy Name wherewith Thou hast taken the covenant of Thine own Self from all Thy servants in Thy Books, Thy Scrolls, and Thy Tablets, to make me, in all conditions, wholly immersed in the ocean of Thy love, uttering Thy praise, and turned toward the Qiblih of Thy bestowals.

order.why: Hear the affirmative answer in the Báb’s words.
shortened: He will raise up creation on a Day when all shall be brought before Him. God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection. This is God's decree wherein there is no doubt. Say: All shall on that Day return unto God, thy Lord.

order.why: End with the translation of belief into constructive deeds and unity.
shortened: The vehicle in this resplendent Age for the practical fulfillment of these duties is the Covenant of Baha'u'llah; it is, indeed, the potent instrument by which individual belief in Him is translated into constructive deeds. The Covenant comprises divinely conceived arrangements necessary to preserve the organic unity of the Cause. It therefore engenders a motivating power which, as the beloved Master tells us, "like unto the artery, beats and pulsates in the body of the world". "It is indubitably clear", He asserts,: "that the pivot of the oneness of mankind is nothing else but the power of the Covenant."

questions: What might it mean to remember a covenant through conduct rather than through recollection alone?
How do the Qur’anic question and the Báb’s discussion of choice shape the meaning of a willing response?
How does the explanation of Alast as the day of manifestation connect primordial language with events in history?
What do the cup, remedy, and tree images disclose about the emotional and spiritual life of a covenant?
How could the final passage’s connection between belief, unity, and constructive deeds change the way one understands fidelity?

neighbors.invitation: Explore how shared reference to the source of a text can protect unity while acknowledging depth of meaning.
Consider the continuing appearance of revelation beyond a fixed number of historical forms.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 7:172 · Humanity’s testimony
references.note: The verse presents the descendants of Adam testifying to God’s lordship so that they cannot plead unawareness at the resurrection. Read it with the compilation’s varied applications of Alast, especially the explanation that connects the question with the day of revelation.

subjects.displayTitle: Divine self-remembrance: praise at the edge of speech
subjects.introduction: He is the Rememberer and the Remembered, the Witness and the Witnessed: Bahá’u’lláh opens tablet after tablet with a paradox that praise cannot climb past. From eternity, He prays, God has described His own Self to His own Self, and no one else can make fitting mention of Him. Whoever sets out to praise God therefore arrives quickly at the edge of speech, and the question is what to do there. The Báb answers that God has cast His likeness into the essence of every created thing, so that all souls are mirrors and whoever truly knows his own self through the attributes of his Creator knows his Lord; the limit becomes a door. The Qur’án, when God declares His own name and oneness, joins that declaration at once to the command to worship and remember [1], and the movement from divine self-disclosure to human response runs through all of this. Reverence of this kind is less self-centred than knowledge, and it opens onto God’s love for His own Essence, the Primal Will and the Word through which He first became known, and the practice of remembrance itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with the rememberer and remembered, explore the limits of praise, follow signs and mirrors, then return to the distinction between divine knowledge and human description.

order.why: Give the theme the intimacy of prayer.
shortened: From eternity Thou didst Thyself describe Thine own Self unto Thy Self, and extol, in Thine own Essence, Thine Essence unto Thine Essence. I swear by Thy glory, O my Best-Beloved! Who is there besides Thee that can claim to know Thee, and who save Thyself can make fitting mention of Thee?

order.why: Open with the paradox of remembrance and names beyond naming.
Concentrate that paradox in witness and witnessed.
shortened: I am the Witness and the Witnessed One.

order.why: Let the brief refrain be heard on its own.
shortened: He is the Rememberer and the Remembered!

order.why: State the limit of knowing the divine essence.
Connect that limit with the created status of all else.
Explore the image of created praise within divinely established bounds.
Read the supplied prayer of befitting praise.
shortened: That which alone beseemeth Thee is the befitting mention made by Thine Own Self, and that only which is worthy of Thee is the anthem of praise voiced by Thine Own Essence....

order.why: Return to the language of revelation as the source of description.
Examine the distinction between divine self-description and description to creatures.
Explore the extended account of signs, souls, and mirrors.
shortened: God described Himself to everything through everything, and cast into the essence of everything His own likeness, until He became known; and in all things there is a sign indicating that He is One.

All souls are as mirrors, and He is manifest to the mirrors through the mirrors. He is the One, the sign of God and His description. And for all things this soul exists - whoso knoweth it hath known his Lord.

The meaning is that there is no way unto God except through recognition of this soul, which is the same as the recognition of the Lord, for a thing cannot be comprehended beyond its source. Whoso knoweth his own self through the attributes of his Creator knoweth Him, and that description is the description of the Lord - there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Most Exalted, the Most Great.

order.why: Consider self-disclosure through the self.
shortened: They who desire to know Him through other than what hath been truthfully revealed are indeed behind a manifest veil. Thus hath He indicated His Own Self through His Own Self.

order.why: Read the imagery of testimony, scripture, and the supreme book.
Hear testimony described before earth and heaven.
shortened: Glorified be He Who testified to His own Self by His own Self before the creation of earth and heaven.

order.why: Consider the limit placed on created knowledge of that testimony.
shortened: God hath in this Day borne witness unto His Own Self by His Own Self that there is no God but Him, and the creation knoweth not a single letter of that testimony, for it is, even as it is, the very essence of testimony in the presence of Divine Unity.

order.why: Read the language of hidden mystery.
Bring testimony into the presence of the living revelation.
Connect self-description with thanksgiving before the servants.
Explains the inadequacy of created descriptions and affirms that God is known and described through Himself.
Notice the movement from divine praise to remembrance of those who follow.
shortened: He remembereth and praiseth His own Self, and remembereth His Afnan after His Aghsan, then those who have held fast unto that which is praiseworthy.

order.why: Return to the supplied testimony before creation.
shortened: God hath testified of His own Self by His own Self before the creation of His heaven and His earth that there is none other God but Him, the Single, the One, the Powerful, the Unconstrained.

order.why: Attend to the repeated language of self-unification and sanctification. Read its complementary formulation without collapsing the distinct excerpt.
shortened: From time immemorial Thou hast been the One Who praiseth Thy Essence through Thy Essence, Who sanctifieth Thy Being through Thy Being, Who uniteth Thy Identity through Thy Identity, Who magnifieth Thy Self through Thy Self. Thou lovest not to be praised except by what Thou art through Thy power, Thy sovereignty, Thy loftiness, and the signs of Thy subsistence.

order.why: Consider praise beyond similitudes, names, and attributes.
Explore the reported mystical stations while keeping their language distinct from an ordinary person’s claims.
shortened: O my beloved! After ascending to the heavens of inner meanings, the wayfarers attain to three stations, meaning that the manifest Sun shines and becomes revealed in the mirrors of existing things according to these three ranks, although some consider the ranks of determinations to be five and have named them the five presences.

In this station and rank, existence is effaced from self and subsists through the Truth. All are from God and unto God shall they return, and "Say: All things are from God" is sufficient witness and adequate proof of this point, as the mystic of Rum has said:

His attributes are annihilated in the attributes of Him
While His essence remains through the survival of His essence

This station certainly has no rules and seeks no customs, meaning all His deeds are pure justice even if outwardly they appear as injustice, and pure knowledge even if in form they appear as ignorance.

questions: How does prayer change when the person praying recognizes that no description can encompass its divine object?
What is gained by repeating the paradoxes of rememberer and remembered, witness and witnessed, rather than resolving them immediately?
How do the images of signs and mirrors make knowledge possible while preserving its limits?
How does the Qur’anic movement from divine self-identification to human worship compare with the movement of these prayers?
How might humility about spiritual knowledge affect the way one speaks about God, oneself, and other people’s understanding?

neighbors.invitation: Consider spiritual growth in discipleship together with the distinction between the disciple and Christ.
Explore the image of an ocean beyond the seas of names.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 20:14 · Declaration and remembrance
references.note: The verse joins God’s self-identification and oneness with the summons to worship and prayerful remembrance. Compare the relation between divine declaration and human response with these passages on God’s self-description; the verse does not by itself set out their full metaphysical account.

subjects.displayTitle: The cloud of unknowing: hiddenness and disclosure
subjects.introduction: Look carefully and you find something; look directly and it is gone. That is how ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes ‘amá, a cloud so light and subtle that it is at once seen and unseen, and he uses it to name the station in which the divine attributes exist in the Essence without yet being distinguished from it, the Hidden Treasure before it is known. Bahá’u’lláh calls it an ocean placed above the seas of names, which no creature has comprehended, and from its Point the letters of revelation are composed. The Báb hears in the word an echo of blindness: a state where nothing existed but God and every eye was veiled. The cloud can also mean the human body of a Prophet, which both carries the light and hides it from those who expect a sun without a sky. At Sinai God tells Moses He will come in a thick cloud so that the people may hear Him speak [1], a kindred pairing of concealment and voice, though the two images need not share one technical sense. Approached with imagination and restraint, the cloud opens onto God’s oneness, His unknowability and transcendence, and the workings of symbolism in sacred language.
subjects.arc: Begin with the subtle cloud’s explanation, explore the emergence of light and utterance, then compare symbolic settings and return to hearing within hiddenness.

order.why: Open with an explanation that gives the difficult term a foothold. Revisit the fuller supplied translation of the opening explanation.
shortened: Al-'Ama' in the language means a very light and subtle cloud that is seen and unseen. If you gaze with utmost care you find something, but as soon as you look, it cannot be seen. That is why, in the tradition of the investigators, by Al-'Ama' they mean the Universal Reality with no specifications, for specifications exist in the mode of simplicity and unity and are not distinguished from the essence. So it is both specified and unspecified, and this station is described as Divine Oneness and Al-'Ama', and it is the station of the Hidden Treasure mentioned in the Hadith.

order.why: Widen the image into an ocean beyond names.
Distinguish divine transcendence from the point of existence and its many names.
shortened: Sanctified is His holy Essence from every abstract essence, and exalted is His pure Countenance above every praise and tribute.

Then, through the requirements of the establishment of the Sovereign of justice upon the throne of mercy and grace, He created, through pure origination and sheer invention, the Point of existence and the Praiseworthy Countenance, which has been expressed through various terms such as the Eternal Countenance, the Divine Reed, the Primal Point, the Warbling of the Dove, the Perfect Word of Manifestation, the Divine Identity of the Cloud of Unknowing, and the Countenance of Ahmad and Muhammad.

order.why: Explore the movement from hidden beauty to visible presence.
Follow the point of the cloud into utterance and letters.
Consider the interaction of tree, leaf, and dove.
Hear a summons to listen within the cloud. Read the parallel summons to hear the Crimson Leaf.
Let the imagery become a brief blessing.
shortened: And shower Thy blessings upon the Mystery of the Cloud, the Point of Light, the Beloved of the mystics.

order.why: Compare another use of cloud as the human appearance that can veil recognition.
shortened: He said the Blessed Perfection, in the Book of Ighan, in explaining the meaning of the statement about Christ coming in heaven and riding on the clouds, says that one meaning of the expression 'cloud', is the body of the prophet.  Why is it that sometimes we cannot see the sun in the sky?  It is because it is veiled from us by thick clouds:  and in this sense, the body, the human nature of a prophet is a cloud, preventing the people from seeing His glorious light.

order.why: Read the recollected conversation as an allegorical exchange.
Explore the Báb’s interpretation of the tradition.
shortened: The word 'ama' (cloud) in the language of the people is related to 'ama (blindness): there, nothing existed but God, and the eyes were blinded from His Face and the gazes from His Countenance. It is an absolute, unmingled, pure cloud, wherein, whether in His hiddenness or His manifestation, His outwardness or His inwardness, naught was seen but God, the One, the Single, the Eternal, the Self-Sufficient, the Peerless, besides Whom there is no other God and with Whom there is none.

order.why: Read the concise supplied wording of the tradition.
Consider the supplied excerpt’s combination of mystery and visible cloud.
shortened: Verily I am the Mystery within mysteries, I was the visible cloud of the Almighty.

O Eternal Tha! All have heard the verses flowing from the attraction of the All-Merciful in wondrous wise, and behold the countenances in the horizon of the divine cloud with the Most Hidden Secret, the Flowing Attractor, made manifest.

order.why: Hear the image as poetic outpouring.
shortened: How excellent is the soaring of this Bird in mentioning the First Solution in the atmosphere of the cloud of unknowing, facing those impenetrable, pitch-dark shadows where none knoweth what it warbleth and concealeth and hideth, save what the All-Merciful willeth in the depths of the mysteries of those hidden, ardent, radiant, and glistening allusions from the lights of the Sun of Glory. Far, far removed are the conjectures of them that conjecture, the deeds of them that act, the attainments of them that attain, and the detachment of them that are detached!

order.why: Follow it into the imagery of light, water, letters, and a point. Consider the image of authorization for explanation.
Places the realm of Ama and the unmixed Point within an explanation of cosmic and letter symbolism.
Read the passage on Joseph and the garment of prophethood.
Explore the symbolic cities and treasuries of eternity.
shortened: Know then that, inasmuch as all the Prophets are but one and the same soul, spirit, name, and attribute, thou must likewise see them all as bearing the name Muhammad and as being the son of Hasan, as having appeared from the Jabulqa of God's power and from the Jabulsa of His mercy. For by Jabulqa is meant none other than the treasure-houses of eternity in the all-highest heaven and the cities of the unseen in the supernal realm.

order.why: Turn to thanksgiving through the image of the nightingale.
shortened: I yield Thee such thanks as can cause the Nightingale of Glory to pour forth its melody in the highest heaven: "'Ali (the Bab), in truth, is Thy servant, Whom Thou hast singled out from among Thy Messengers and Thy chosen Ones, and made Him to be the Manifestation of Thyself in all that pertaineth unto Thee, and that concerneth the revelation of Thine attributes and the evidences of Thy names."

order.why: Keep the secondary scholarly account distinct from the primary voices.
Bring the imagery into the scene of Sinai and hidden song.
Hear the invitation to emerge into light.
Close with hearing a divine call without claiming to have seen its source.

questions: How does the image of something seen and then unseen help you approach the relation between unity and distinction?
What different work does cloud do when it signifies a hidden source, a realm of revelation, or the human appearance that can veil recognition?
How does the cloud and voice at Sinai illuminate these images, and where should the comparison remain open?
What changes when a passage moves from explaining the cloud to singing, praying, or speaking from within its imagery?
How can a reader explore these difficult passages imaginatively while respecting differences of translation, source, and interpretive authority?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the relation between divine hiddenness and the signs available within created things.
Consider how to share an illuminating personal reading without making it a binding standard.

references.label: 1 · Exodus 19:9 · A voice within the cloud
references.note: At Sinai, God tells Moses that the cloud will accompany speech that the people can hear. Compare this narrative relation of hiddenness, hearing, and trust with the varied uses of ‘amá here; a shared image need not carry an identical technical meaning.
